q: The mandate of LTO is to register roadworthy and emission-compliant motor vehicles, put order on the roads, and to ____________ .
A: observe cleanliness on the road
C: formulate franchising guidelines of PUVs
info: LTO's mandates under RA 4136 are registering roadworthy, emission-compliant vehicles and licensing quality drivers for road order.

q: What is the maximum penalty for a habitual violator of R.A. 10666 also known as Children’s Safety on Motorcycle Act?
A: Imprisonment of six years
C: Revocation of driver’s license
info: RA 10666 punishes habitual violators most severely with license revocation to remove repeat child-endangering riders.

q: What does this traffic sign means?
A: Approach to intersection
C: Merging traffic ahead
imageDesc: Red-bordered triangular warning sign with black cross-intersection symbol (straight arrow crossed by horizontal bar)
info: Red-bordered triangle is a warning sign; the cross symbol warns of an intersection ahead, so slow down.

q: After turning right from an intersection into a one-way street, which lane should you choose?
A: Stay on the rightmost lane
C: Stay on the center of the road
info: Turn into the nearest/rightmost lane on a one-way to stay predictable and avoid cutting across traffic.

q: A person with disability can possess a driver’s license if:
A: the driving conditions are indicated on the DL
B: it is expressly written on the student permit
C: he/she is accompanied by a qualified instructor
info: A PWD may be licensed if needed adaptations/conditions are indicated on the DL, proving safe operation.

q: What is the meaning of this traffic light?
A: Stop before the stop line
B: Continue driving if there is no obstruction
C: Stop as directed by the traffic enforcer
imageDesc: Vertical traffic light with the top red light illuminated
info: Steady red means full stop before the stop line and wait for green; it is the mandatory stop signal.

q: Under which of these circumstances it is permissible to use a mobile phone while driving a motor vehicle?
A: If it is an important call
C: None of the above
info: Handheld phone use while driving is prohibited in all listed cases under the Anti-Distracted Driving Act.

q: What should you do if a traffic police officer directed you to drive through a red light or stop sign?
A: You must not obey or you will be apprehended
C: You must ignore the police and wait for the green light. This is in accordance with traffic enforcer’s implementing rules and regulations
info: A traffic officer's direction overrides lights and signs, so you must obey for orderly, safe flow.

q: What is the meaning of this traffic sign?
A: Speed limit on this area must not be less than 60 kph
B: Speed limit on this area is 60 kph
C: This zone is 60 km long
imageDesc: Square white sign with red circle containing number 60 and the word ZONE below
info: Red circle means prohibition/regulation; this ZONE sign caps speed at 60 kph throughout the zone.

q: It is more dangerous to turn left than to turn right because ____________ .
A: the road has lanes
B: vehicles coming from opposite direction are faster
C: there are more vendors on the right side of the road
info: Left turns cross the path of faster oncoming traffic, making gaps harder to judge and crashes likelier.

q: A driver must not park or stop at the side of the road of a “Stop” sign when it is within:
A: 3 meters
C: 6 meters
info: RA 4136 Sec 46 bans parking within 6m of an intersection or Stop sign to preserve sight distance.

q: What does this sign mean?
A: No entry
C: No through road
imageDesc: Red circular sign with white horizontal bar in the center
info: Red circle with white bar is a prohibitory No Entry sign; entering risks head-on collision.

q: Changing lanes at an intersection is:
A: very safe
C: unsafe
info: Intersections have crossing and turning conflicts, so changing lanes there is unsafe and prohibited.

q: Parking is allowed if the vehicle is:
A: beyond 4 meters of a fire hydrant
B: within 3 meters of the intersection of curve lines
C: within an intersection
info: RA 4136 Sec 46 bans parking within 4m of a hydrant; beyond 4m keeps it accessible to firefighters.

q: What does this traffic sign means?
A: Minumum speed 30 kph
C: End of minimum Speed
imageDesc: Blue circular sign with white 30 crossed by a red diagonal line
info: As the video teaches it: blue means minimum/mandatory speed, so the crossed blue 30 means End of minimum Speed.

q: You can overtake in a highway if it has two lanes with:
A: broken white lines
C: continuous yellow line
info: Broken white lines may be crossed when safe, so overtaking is allowed; continuous lines prohibit crossing.

q: What is the appropriate action if you feel sleepy while driving?
A: Turn on the radio very loudly
C: Park at a rest stop and rest
info: Fatigue slows reaction like alcohol; park at a rest stop and rest to avoid falling asleep at the wheel.

q: What does this traffic sign means?
A: Downhill course
C: Humps ahead
imageDesc: Red-bordered triangular warning sign with black arrow pointing up a slope
info: Red triangle is a warning sign; the upslope arrow warns of an uphill course, so adjust gear and speed.

q: The Temporary Operator's Permit (TOP) authorizes the apprehended driver to operate motor vehicle for a period not exceeding:
A: 72 hours
C: 15 days
info: A TOP is only a 72-hour temporary authority to drive while the apprehension is settled.

q: Double broken white lines on the road means:
A: it is prohibited to overtake on the left side
B: it is prohibited to overtake on the right side
C: you are allowed to overtake on the left or right if there is no danger
info: Double broken white lines may be crossed, so overtaking on left or right is allowed if there is no danger.

q: Who is responsible for not overloading vehicle?
A: The driver or rider of the vehicle
B: The person who loaded the vehicle
C: The owner of the vehicle
info: The driver/rider controls loading and operation, so they are responsible for refusing overload per RA 4136.

q: What does this traffic sign means?
A: Slippery road
C: Curve road
imageDesc: Red triangular warning sign with black skidding-car icon and wavy skid marks
info: The skidding-car with wavy marks warns of low traction, so slow down and avoid sudden braking.

q: What does the law require you to do upon approaching an intersection with a stop sign?
A: Yield right-of-way if necessary to vehicles approaching from left to right
B: Stop and proceed when it is safe to do so
C: Slow down and proceed when it is safe to do so
info: A stop sign requires a full stop; proceed only when safe per RA 4136.

q: A blue traffic sign says “60 kph”. What should you do?
A: Drive at a maximum of 60 kph
B: Drive at a minimum of 60 kph
C: Drive at 60 minutes per kilometer
info: Blue signs give minimums, so blue 60 kph means drive at minimum 60 kph.

q: What should you do when the brake lights of the vehicle in front of you activates?
A: Prepare to brake
C: Turn right or left
info: Brake lights mean the vehicle ahead is slowing, so prepare to brake and keep distance.

q: What does this traffic sign means?
A: Approach to intersection merging traffic
C: Approach to highway
imageDesc: Red triangular warning sign with black icon of a side road joining from the right
info: The side-junction symbol shows a minor road joining from the right, so expect merging traffic.

q: Road rage is violent anger caused by the stress and frustration involved in driving a motor vehicle in difficult conditions, especially when the driver is experiencing ______________.
A: heavy traffic of gridlock
C: light traffic along a busy road
info: Road rage is stress-driven anger, most triggered by heavy traffic or gridlock frustration.

q: You may drive over a pathway ______________.
A: if no pedestrian are near
C: to overtake slow-moving traffic
info: Footways are for pedestrians; you may only cross one to get into a property or driveway.

q: What does this sign mean?
A: You can park on the days shown
C: No parking at all from Monday to Friday
imageDesc: Rectangular no-parking sign with crossed-out P, text ANYTIME Mon-Fri and double-headed arrow
info: The crossed P with ANYTIME Mon-Fri bans parking on that stretch all day Monday to Friday.

q: Where should you install your saddle bag or box?
A: Not more than 10 cm higher than the rider's seat
C: Not higher than the rider's seat
info: A high box unbalances a motorcycle, so the saddle bag must not be higher than the rider's seat.

q: The vehicle is parked if:
A: it is not moving while loading passengers
B: it is not moving while unloading passengers
C: it is at stand and the engine is turned off
info: Parked means at a stand with engine off, not merely stopped to load or unload.

q: What does this traffic sign means?
A: Dangerous left double curve
C: Dangerous right double curve
imageDesc: Red-bordered triangular warning sign with black winding double-curve arrow to the right
info: The double-curve arrow to the right warns of a dangerous right double curve; slow down.

q: The proper hand signal for a left turn is:
A: left arm straight in horizontal position
B: left arm at elbow hand pointing up
C: left hand down and hang pointing to the ground
info: Standard hand signal for left turn is left arm extended straight out horizontally.

q: Where should you position your vehicle when you are planning to turn left into a minor road?
A: In the middle of the road
B: On the rightmost part of the road
C: On the leftmost part of the road
info: To turn left without cutting across traffic, position on the leftmost part of the road.

q: What do you mean by “double white line” line?
A: To pass a vehicle that is towing a trailer
B: To pass traffic is queuing back at junction
C: Separating lanes of traffic moving from opposite direction
info: Double white line separates lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

q: You approach a junction. The traffic lights are not working. A traffic enforcer gives this signal. You should:
A: stop at the stop line
C: stop level with the officer’s arm
imageDesc: Photo of a traffic enforcer in yellow uniform with right arm raised straight up
info: Raised-arm stop signal with dead lights means halt; stop at the stop line.

q: A “No Stopping” sign means you:
A: can stop quickly if you are loading or unloading a passenger
B: cannot stop unless receiving a call
C: cannot stop unless directed by a traffic officer
info: No Stopping is stricter than No Parking; you cannot stop unless directed by a traffic officer.

q: This traffic sign means “Yield the right-of-way”:
A: inverted triangle
C: horizontal triangle
info: Yield right-of-way is the inverted point-down triangle; give way to priority traffic.

q: The choice of the speed may depend on the:
A: roadworthiness of the motor vehicle being driven
C: all of the above
info: Safe speed depends on vehicle roadworthiness, road, traffic and driver skill, so all of the above.

q: What is the meaning of this traffic sign?
A: No entry for vehicles with 30 years age
C: End of maximum speed limit
imageDesc: White sign with text END above a red-circled 60 speed limit symbol
info: END over a 60 limit cancels it, so it means end of maximum speed limit.

q: Single white broken line on a two (2) way lane road means:
A: passing or overtaking can be made anytime
C: it separates traffic moving in opposite directions
info: Broken center line separates opposing traffic on a two-way road; it marks lanes but may be crossed to overtake only when clear.

q: What should be done first before changing lanes?
A: Make a quick change of lane
B: Check the traffic ahead and make signal
C: Blow your horn then carefully change lane
info: Check traffic and signal first to warn others and confirm a safe gap; sudden lane changes cause side collisions.

q: What does this traffic sign means?
A: Road works
C: Uneven light signals ahead
imageDesc: Triangular warning sign with red border showing a worker digging with a shovel
info: Red-bordered triangles are warning signs; the digging-worker symbol means road works ahead, so slow down and prepare to maneuver.

q: While driving on a one way direction, you intend to turn left into a minor road. On the approach you should:
A: keep in the middle of the road
B: swing out wide just before turning
C: keep well to the left of the road
info: On a one-way road keep well left to turn left so you stay on your turning side, shorten the turn and avoid cutting across others.

q: What should you do if a railroad crossing has no warning devices?
A: Increase your speed and cross the tracks quickly but do not forget to wear helmet
B: Stop within 15 feet of the railroad crossing, get out of the vehicle, walk through the railroad and check if it is clear
C: Slow down, check left and right of the railroad, and then proceed with caution if clear
info: With no bells or lights, slow down, look both ways and cross only if clear, because trains cannot stop quickly.

q: A vehicle that enters a roadway from a driveway, alley, or a private road:
A: must stop and yield the right-of-way to traffic on the roadway and pedestrians
B: has the right-of-way to traffic from all directions
C: has the right-of-way to traffic especially from the left side of the street
info: Under RA 4136, vehicles from a driveway, alley or private road must stop and yield since through-road traffic and pedestrians have priority.

q: What does this traffic sign means?
A: One way ahead
C: Narrow bridge ahead
imageDesc: Blue rectangular sign with a large white arrow pointing straight up
info: Blue signs give mandatory direction information; the straight-up white arrow means one-way ahead, so go only in that direction.

q: What is the primary purpose of using the vehicle's horn?
A: To make beautiful sounds for all motorist to hear
B: To create noise and avoid distractions
C: To give warning to avoid road crash
info: The horn is a safety device, not for noise; use it only to warn others to avoid a road crash.

q: You were invited to a dinner party. You know that you will have to drive afterwards. What is your best course of action?
A: Eat a hot meal with your alcohol drink
C: Not drink any alcohol at all
info: Any alcohol impairs judgment and reflexes, so if you must drive, drink nothing at all — food or mixing drinks does not make you safe.

q: What should you do when you see this traffic light?
A: Go ahead
C: Go if there is no obstruction on the other side
imageDesc: Vertical traffic light with the bottom green light illuminated
info: A steady green means go; proceed through if the way is clear and yield as required for turns or pedestrians.

q: What must you do at a flashing yellow traffic signal?
A: This signal tells you that you cannot turn at this intersection, so continue on straight
B: Drive with caution, consider it as a "Give Way" sign
C: Stop, yield, and proceed when safe
info: Flashing yellow means proceed with caution as a Give Way sign; slow down, yield to conflicting traffic and go when safe.

q: Drinking alcohol before driving is one of the major causes of vehicular road crash because when a driver is drunk he/she is:
A: arrogant, talkative, with poor judgment and reflexes to perform things safely
B: calm, relaxed, and able to perform things accordingly
C: able to talk intelligently and coherently and give every appearance of sobriety
info: Alcohol causes arrogance, poor judgment and slow reflexes, which is why drunk driving is a leading cause of fatal crashes.

q: To drive on the road, one must have these documents ready:
A: DL and Registration and Insurance Policy
B: Valid DL and Updated Registration and Insurance Policy
C: CPC and Fare Matrix
info: PH rules require a valid DL plus updated vehicle registration and insurance; all three prove you and the vehicle are legal to run.

q: What does this traffic sign means?
A: Steep left curve
C: Dangerous right
imageDesc: Red-bordered triangular warning sign with a black arrow bending sharply to the left
info: Red-bordered triangles warn of hazards; the sharp left-bending arrow means a steep left curve ahead, so slow down and stay in lane.

q: You must not blow the horn of your vehicle unless:
A: a moving vehicle may cause you danger
B: you want to call the attention of a traffic enforcer
C: you want to signal your arrival
info: Use the horn only as a crash warning when another moving vehicle may endanger you, not to call attention or announce arrival.

q: Someone is waiting to cross at pedestrian crossing. They are standing on the pavement. You should normally:
A: go on quickly before they step onto the crossing
B: stop, let them cross, wait patiently
C: ignore them as they are still on the pavements
info: Pedestrians have priority at crossings; stop and wait patiently so they can cross safely even if still on the pavement.

q: What is the meaning of this traffic sign?
A: Local speed limit applies
C: Speed limit applies / Speed de-restriction
imageDesc: Circular white sign with a single thick black diagonal stripe
info: The white circle with diagonal stripe ends a special limit; standard speed limits apply again, so adjust speed accordingly.

q: When being overtaken by a car, what should you do?
A: Increase speed to avoid being overtaken
C: Press on the brake and allow the overtaking vehicle to pass
info: Hold your speed when overtaken to stay predictable; accelerating or braking hard forces the overtaking car into danger.

q: A traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?
A: Keep going at your current speed
B: Stop, even if in the intersection
C: Stop before the intersection or stop line
info: Yellow after green warns red is next; stop before the intersection or stop line and do not beat the red light.

q: What does this traffic sign means?
A: Dangerous right double bend
C: Dangerous curve
imageDesc: Red-bordered triangular warning sign with a black winding S-shaped double-bend arrow
info: Red-bordered triangles are warnings; the S-shaped arrow means dangerous left double bend ahead, so slow down and keep lane discipline.
